Aggregate root architecture by order, or by groups of orders

Source: R/RootBranching.R
order_metrics.Rd

Flexible query over a branch_order_map result (or its $edges table): length, diameter, and branching architecture, either one row per order class or one row per named group of orders. Diameter is length-weighted so it reflects how much root length sits at each width. Lengths/diameters are in the unit of x; counts are integers; branching_frequency is per unit length.

Usage

order_metrics(x, order_col = NULL, groups = NULL, focal = NULL)

Arguments

x

A "branchOrderMap" object or an edges data.frame.

order_col

Order column to aggregate by; defaults to the object's $order, else "order_from_base". A deprecated alias resolves to the column it names.

groups

How to pool orders into rows:

  • NULL (default): one row per order class, ascending.

  • A named list of order sets, e.g. list(fine = 1:2, coarse = 3:5). Each element holds values of order_col and its name becomes the group label. Orders that no element lists are pooled into one extra row named "rest", so every ordered segment is counted exactly once; when nothing is left over that row is absent, and a group that catches no segment gets no row. Naming one order in two groups is an error.

  • "thinnest" or "thickest": the one order class with the smallest or largest length-weighted diameter, with the others pooled into "rest". The pick is by diameter, so it does not depend on how the orders are numbered; the orders column reports which order number(s) landed in each row.

focal

Deprecated alias for groups; it warns. A numeric value or vector is read as groups = list(focal = focal); "thinnest", "thickest" and the aliases "finest" / "coarsest" are read as the matching groups string.

Value

A data.frame with one row per order class or per group:

first column

Named after order_col and holding the order value when groups is NULL; named group and holding the group label otherwise.

orders

Comma-separated order numbers contained in the group. Present only when groups is given.

n_segments

Graph segments in the row.

n_tips

Root tips/apices (degree-1 endpoints).

n_branch_points

Branching junctions on roots of the row.

total_length

Summed root length.

length_fraction

Share of total ordered length.

cumulative_length

Running total of total_length over the rows above and including this one. Present only when groups is NULL, where the rows ascend in the order value.

cumulative_fraction

cumulative_length over the total ordered length, so the last row is 1. Present under the same condition.

mean_segment_length

Mean length per segment.

branching_frequency

Branch points per unit length.

mean_diameter

Length-weighted mean diameter.

median_diameter

Median of segment median diameters.

An order class with no segments has no row, so the per-order rows can skip values; the cumulative columns step from one present order to the next rather than inserting a zero, which would drag down any mean taken over the rows. attr(., "n_unordered") counts NA-order segments. When groups is given, attr(., "groups") holds the resolved list of order sets, "rest" included.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- branch_order_map(skel, mask, order = "order_from_base", unit = "cm", dpi = 300)
order_metrics(res)                                   # per-order table
order_metrics(res, groups = list(fine = 1:2))        # orders 1-2 vs "rest"
order_metrics(res, groups = list(fine = 1:2, coarse = 3:4))
order_metrics(res, groups = "thinnest")              # thinnest class vs "rest"
} # }
